Section 5 • \(P\)3D

5.5 Reduction to the 1D power spectrum, \(\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}(k_\parallel)\)

In configuration space the 1D 2PCF is the evaluation of the 3D one at \(\vec{r}_\perp=\vec{0}\) (Eq. (4.11)). In Fourier space the roles are exchanged: the 1D power spectrum is the integral of the 3D one over all \(\vec{k}_\perp\). As in Sec. 4, we start from the per-sightline objects, whose first argument is a position. The 1D Fourier transform and periodogram of the sightline at \(\vec{x}_\perp\) are \begin{align} \widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s),\rm 1D}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp;k_\parallel\right) &\equiv \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b}\! d\Lambda\; e^{-ik_\parallel\Lambda}\, \delta_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right), \notag\\ \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s),\rm 1D}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp;k_\parallel\right) &\equiv \frac{2\pi}{L_\Lambda}\, \widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s),\rm 1D}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp;k_\parallel\right)\, \widetilde{\delta}_j^{(s),\rm 1D}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp;k_\parallel\right)^*, \tag{5.13} \end{align} and the 1D power spectrum is their average over sightlines, \(\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}(k_\parallel)\equiv|\mathcal{A}_\perp|^{-1}\int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}d^2x_\perp\, \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s),\rm 1D}(\vec{x}_\perp;k_\parallel)\). Step by step:

  1. Comparing with Eq. (5.1), the 3D transform is the 2D transverse transform of the per-sightline one: \(\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}(\vec{k}_\perp,k_\parallel)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}d^2x_\perp\, e^{-i\vec{k}_\perp\cdot\vec{x}_\perp}\,\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s),\rm 1D}(\vec{x}_\perp;k_\parallel)\).

  2. Parseval’s theorem in the transverse plane (with the fields set to zero outside \(\mathcal{A}_\perp\)) then gives \(\int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}d^2x_\perp\,\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s),\rm 1D}\,\widetilde{\delta}_j^{(s),\rm 1D\,*} =\int d^2k_\perp\,\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}(\vec{k}_\perp,k_\parallel)\,\widetilde{\delta}_j^{(s)}(\vec{k}_\perp,k_\parallel)^*\).

  3. Multiplying by \(2\pi/(|\mathcal{A}_\perp|L_\Lambda)\) and using Eq. (5.2), \(\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}\widetilde{\delta}_j^{(s)*}=|\mathcal{A}_\perp|L_\Lambda\,\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}/(2\pi)^3\):

\begin{align} \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(k_\parallel\right) \equiv \frac{1}{|\mathcal{A}_\perp|}\int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}\! d^2x_\perp\; \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s),\rm 1D}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp;k_\parallel\right) &= \int\!\frac{d^2k_\perp}{(2\pi)^2}\; \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{k}_{\perp},k_\parallel\right) \notag\\ &= \frac{1}{(2\pi)^2}\int_0^\infty\! dk_\perp\,k_\perp\; \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(k_\perp,k_\parallel\right), \tag{5.14} \end{align} exact for every realization, the last form with Eq. (5.6). The 1D power spectrum therefore receives contributions from all transverse modes, and is a projection of the 3D one, even though the 1D 2PCF is a slice. Eq. (5.3) carries over unchanged, \(\widehat{P}_{ji}^{(s)}(k_\parallel)=\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}(k_\parallel)^*=\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}(-k_\parallel)\).

Fourier link.

Integrating Eq. (5.4) over \(\vec{k}_\perp\), \(\int d^2k_\perp\,e^{i\vec{k}_\perp\cdot\vec{r}_\perp}/(2\pi)^2=\delta_{\rm D}^{(2)}(\vec{r}_\perp)\) selects \(\vec{r}_\perp=\vec{0}\), where \(\overline{W}(\vec{0},\Delta)=1-|\Delta|/L_\Lambda\): \begin{equation} \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(k_\parallel\right) = \int_{-L_\Lambda}^{L_\Lambda}\! d\Delta\; \left(1-\frac{|\Delta|}{L_\Lambda}\right)\, \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\Delta\right)\, e^{+ik_\parallel\Delta}, \tag{5.15} \end{equation} with \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\Delta)\) of Eq. (4.11) and, for \(\Delta<0\), \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\Delta)=\widehat{\xi}_{ji}^{(s)}(-\Delta)\) (Eq. (4.3)). The same result follows by averaging over sightlines the exact per-sightline relation between \(\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s),\rm 1D}\) and \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s),\rm 1D}\). The two reductions thus close a commuting diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{array}{ccc} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{r}_\perp,\Delta\right) & \xrightarrow{\ \text{Eq.~(\href{relation-to-the-per-sample-3d-2pcf.html#eq:Pk3D_from_xi3D_sample}{5.4})}\ } & \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{k}_\perp,k_\parallel\right) \\[4pt] \Big\downarrow\;\vec{r}_\perp=\vec{0} & & \Big\downarrow\;\int d^2k_\perp/(2\pi)^2 \\[4pt] \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\Delta\right) & \xrightarrow{\ \text{Eq.~(\href{#eq:Pk3D_P1D_from_xi1D}{5.15})}\ } & \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(k_\parallel\right) \end{array} \tag{5.16} \end{equation} Conversely, evaluating the 3D power spectrum at \(\vec{k}_\perp=\vec{0}\) corresponds to integrating the 2PCF over \(\vec{r}_\perp\), i.e. to the correlation of the transverse-averaged fields, which is not the 1D power spectrum (Fig. 11).
